columns.cast.anchor_line: def _column_type(column: ColumnSpec) -> Any:  # noqa: ANN401 - dynamic pydantic field type
columns.cast.why: _column_type maps a declared kind onto one pydantic domain, so the engine enforces a value's type but never converts epoch milliseconds or reformats a published date.

columns.derive.why: A column's value is copied out of the record verbatim; no column is computed from other columns, concatenated, or parsed out of a symbol.

columns.null_sentinel.why: A column can declare that it may be null but not which raw spellings -- the strings 'None', '0' or empty -- become null, so per-row sentinel nulling is a fetcher behaviour the engine cannot express.

columns.rename.why: Every column declares the raw key it reads and publishes it under its own name.

columns.rescale.why: ColumnSpec keeps units verbatim for the review record and applies nothing, so a published percent or a 1/1000 strike scale cannot be declared.

columns.response_dependent_selection.why: Each column reads exactly one declared source key, and the columns it may read are a fixed tuple written before the request. A row whose columns are whichever XBRL tags this issuer happened to publish cannot be declared; columns.select covers a static selection, which is why the SEC statement rows carry both labels.

columns.select.why: normalize_record walks only the declared columns and the generated row model forbids extras, so an undeclared raw key cannot reach a row.

decode.archive_member.why: One named member is selected from the archive (exact, then basename, then glob) and its bytes handed to the delimited reader -- only for a zip_csv body; an archive of XML or XLSX has no decoder kind.

decode.delimited.anchor_line: for row in csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""), delimiter=delimiter)
decode.delimited.why: decode_body reads csv/tsv/zip_csv bytes into header-keyed rows with a declarable delimiter, member and encoding.

decode.delimited_headerless.why: preamble_rows lets a body put non-blank rows before its header, but what follows is still read as the header and HEADER_MISMATCH fires when it names none of the declared columns. A body that publishes no header at all, whose columns are positional, has no declaration surface -- decode.delimited names a present decoder kind, not this.

decode.geojson.why: A feature collection publishes its attributes under geometry members; no kind walks them into rows.

decode.html_table.why: No html kind exists, so an HTML table cannot be declared as a body shape.

decode.html_text.why: No html kind exists, and the engine never strips markup or rewrites a body as markdown.

decode.opaque_bytes.why: A body becomes a document or it becomes rows; no kind publishes the bytes themselves as the result, which is what a PDF download needs.

decode.tabular_file.why: No workbook kind exists in the decoder vocabulary and nothing reads a sheet region.

decode.text_table.why: Only a delimited reader splits a body; a colon-delimited file or a regex-parsed line has no decoder kind.

decode.xml.why: The decoder vocabulary is a closed Literal and DecoderSpec.__post_init__ rejects anything outside it, so no declaration can ask for an XML or RSS body.

flow.branch.why: One base_url and one path string per declaration: an interval/metric/region branch that addresses different endpoints has no declaration surface.

flow.composite_key_segment.why: ModelSpec.composite_keys holds one CompositeKeySpec per composed placeholder and render_path routes that placeholder through ``_render_composite``, which joins the declared positions and refuses any result that could break out of one segment. The scalar branch still gates on _PATH_SEGMENT, which omits the comma, so a comma-joined key is legal only through a composition whose separator the kernel checked.

flow.fan_out.why: fetch_pages builds one URL per declaration and pages it; there is no per-symbol or per-item request set to enumerate and concatenate.

flow.join.why: The same single-URL loop is the proof no second response is fetched and joined onto the first model's rows.

flow.preflight_lookup.why: The URL is known from the declaration before any request, so a directory lookup that decides the URL afterwards cannot be declared.

flow.url_template.why: render_path substitutes each declared {placeholder} from the validated query, after _PATH_SEGMENT proves the value is exactly one URL segment.

outside.anti_bot.why: _classify_status maps a throttled status onto a stable failure code and raises it; a retry-and-warm-up loop is not the engine's semantics.

outside.bespoke.why: Delegation to or composition of a hand-written fetcher is recorded in each provider's NOT_DECLARABLE ledger instead of being built into the engine.

outside.no_request.why: A declaration must name an https origin, so a model that only transposes a bundled constant has no static-source field to use.

outside.sdk.anchor: Nothing in this package performs I/O or imports an upstream SDK.
outside.sdk.anchor_line: Nothing in this package performs I/O or imports an upstream SDK.
outside.sdk.why: A model whose answer is an SDK call cannot be expressed as a declaration at all; the engine forbids SDK imports by design, so this is delegation rather than engine work.

outside.source_absent.why: A vendored upstream tree that is not in the repo is a filesystem fact this instrument does not read; recorded unanchored rather than anchored to a token whose absence would be indistinguishable from a typo.

outside.stateful.why: Headers a declaration sends are static pairs replayed on every page, so a cookie warmed by a prior response or a local cache store has nowhere to live.

param.preset_merge.why: ``params`` is a fixed declared tuple with no field that merges a preset filter set into the caller's parameters, which is what a screener built from a preset ini needs.

param.value_mapping.why: ParamSpec.value_map declares the (caller, upstream) pairs and ``_apply_value_map`` runs them at encode time, refusing a value the map does not spell rather than sending the caller's own text. Presence is measured from both lines, so the face moves with the code.

param.value_transform.why: The key may be renamed while the value is substituted verbatim once validated, so a rule that strips a leading '$' or appends ':US' when no exchange suffix is present cannot be declared -- only hardcoded in a fetcher.

path.assemble_single_row.why: normalize_record builds exactly one row out of exactly one record, so a model whose single row is assembled from many values has nowhere to say so.

path.explode.anchor_line: def resolve_rows(document: object, pointer: str, spec: ModelSpec) -> list[Any]:
path.explode.why: One pointer returns one record list; nothing re-reads the document per record, expands a nested array into rows, or pivots a series.

path.object_keys.why: A document that is not a JSON array is refused, so records keyed by object member or flattened out of a graph cannot be located.

path.parameterized_pointer.why: Both read sites hand resolve_rows one declaration-time string, spec.rows_pointer, so the pointer cannot depend on the response or on a query field. TMX keeps its rows under indices[query.symbol], which is a pointer built per request rather than a fixed dotted path; the dotted walker itself runs fine, it just has nothing to be handed here.

request.body.why: Names the engine's only send seam: _http_get_json calls the governed client's GET. The GET-only call is the proof that no request body can be declared.

request.body_pagination.why: An offset is written into the query keys and never into a body, so body-driven offset paging is not expressible.

request.caller_url.why: One declared path string filled by placeholders: no field accepts a caller-supplied URL, and ``render_path`` refuses any substituted value that is not exactly one segment, so a model addressed by a URL the caller brings cannot be declared -- and would be an SSRF seam if it could.

request.graphql.why: The same GET-only send seam is the proof there is no query-template request shape.

request.serialised_param.why: _encode_value renders a list parameter by comma-joining it; nothing serialises a JSON object or a key/date mapping into one query value.

rows.filter.anchor_line: row_filters: Client-side selections applied after the source's own completeness was judged;
rows.filter.why: Presence is read off the disk rather than asserted: row_filters is the field only a finished client-side row filter can add to ModelSpec, so this entry reports absent until it lands and present from the first run after it does.

rows.order_limit.why: _page_request adds paging keys and nothing else: rows stay in upstream order, with no sort and no top-n applied.

shape.columnar.why: Parallel arrays under named keys are a dict, and resolve_rows only accepts a list.

shape.nested_data_message.why: SDMX-JSON needs message shaping (dimension series, observation keys, sectioned structure); the engine reads a JSON document or a delimited table and nothing else.

method_note: Measured this round: the census rows were read from the census-*.json files, every needs_engine_capability label was mapped through LABEL_TO_CAPABILITY (an unmapped label aborts the run), each registry claim was checked by reading its proof_file for its anchor token, and production declaration counts came from an AST scan of opendata/data/providers minus _engine/ and minus _vendor/. Carried forward from the census files: provider, upstream_model, expressible_today and the need lists themselves. Carried forward by construction: the label map and every anchor string. No engine code was executed, no recorded fixture was replayed, and no request was made; a capability this round cannot claim more than that its source text exists.
